source_text: Ostendi certe non nos aliud defendere, quam quod primo ratio signat aequissimum, tum etiam Deus sua lege confirmat, tertio non aliter quam asserimus, id quod fuerat praeceptum, cum operis laude completum. Inculcatum est quoque hanc veram esse iustitiam, quam placere sibi Deus etiam praecipiendo monstravit. Ac per hoc constitit nihil adminiculi Manichaeam traducem aut in ratione aut in legis testimoniis invenire.
pass_a_gloss: I have certainly shown that we defend nothing other than what first reason marks as most fair, then also God confirms by his law, thirdly that what had been precepted was completed with praise of the work not otherwise than we assert. It has also been impressed that this is true justice, which God has shown to please him even by precepting. And through this it has stood that the Manichaean vine-layer finds no support either in reason or in the testimonies of the law.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: I have certainly shown that what we defend is nothing other than what reason first identifies as entirely fair, what God then confirms in his law, and what, thirdly, was carried out with praise for the deed, precisely as we maintain the command should be understood. I have also repeatedly emphasized that this is true justice, which God showed to be pleasing to him by commanding it. Thus it has been established that the Manichaean transmission of sin finds no support either in reason or in the law’s testimonies (Deuteronomy 24:16) (2 Kings 14:5–6).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied.
